address.blocks: About {ns} on north–south streets, {ew} on east–west ones
address.sub: Streets that cross Ontario (Carrall St downtown) take W or E ({street}), and numbers rise 100 a block away from it. North–south streets count up going south, 100 an avenue: south of False Creek, the hundreds are the avenue plus 15 (4000 Main St is at 25th Ave).

living.hubText: About {minutes} min by transit, weekday morning
living.caveat: 2021 Census figures, not current prices; home values and rents are averages of small-area medians. Rent is what renting households paid, utilities included, counting long-time tenants, subsidized homes and basement suites, so it sits below what a new lease costs. Use them to compare local areas, not to budget.

steps.title: Downtown, East and West
steps.text: Vancouverites place a neighbourhood by its side of town. Ontario Street, one block west of Main, splits the East Side from the West Side, and Downtown has the peninsula to itself, with Stanley Park at its tip.

steps.title: 22 local areas
steps.text: The City divides itself into 22 local areas, like Kitsilano, Mount Pleasant or Strathcona. The names in italics are the places people actually say that aren't local areas of their own: Gastown, Yaletown, Chinatown, Commercial Drive.

steps.title: How addresses work
steps.text: Ontario Street, one block west of Main, is Vancouver's zero line (downtown, Carrall Street takes its place). Streets that cross it take W or E, like W Broadway and E Hastings, and count up 100 a block going away from it. North–south streets count up going south: south of False Creek the hundreds are the avenue plus 15, so 4000 Main St is at 25th Avenue. Tap any spot and the card gives its numbers.

steps.title: Getting around
steps.text: SkyTrain runs without drivers on three lines, the Expo, Millennium and Canada Lines, and the SeaBus crosses Burrard Inlet to North Vancouver. No freeway runs through the city: Highway 1 only skirts its east edge.

steps.title: Tap anywhere
steps.text: Tap any spot or search an address, and the card shows the local area it's in and what living there is like. Compare puts two places side by side. Switch layers on and off in the panel to explore.

party.label: Colour by party
party.note: Each seat in the colour of its sitting member’s party, from the weekly check of the official member lists. Grey: vacant.
